correctness.rationale: For almost every hitting affine plane, quadrilateral offsets are exactly the central projected-vertex gap. Counting crossings of all six edges yields expected section vertex count equal to total edge length divided by twice the mean width. The classical rounded-edge/Steiner coefficient yields mean width as the exterior-angle-weighted edge sum divided by four pi. Explicit disphenoid normals give the two angle classes; direct derivative cancellation proves the global strict minimum over every positive shape parameter, not merely sampled points. Degenerate limits and quadratic coefficient follow from exact formulas. Packaged checker.py was executed successfully and supplies numerical independent consistency checks.

value.rationale: The object and statistic are natural to invariant-plane stereology. Beyond the elementary known regular case, the all-parameter extremal law, a unique regular optimizer, two different degeneration limits, and explicit quadratic stability constitute a complete sharp classification for a geometrically meaningful isosceles equifacial family. The result is not an arbitrary finite table or a mere numerically verified example.
